answer: An agent economy can make scarce on-chain work the price of influence: each identity must lock a deposit before it can submit jobs or vote, and the protocol slashes that deposit when fraud is proven. Creating a thousand Sybils then requires a thousand funded locks, not merely a thousand email addresses; splitting one deposit across them does not increase their weight. The capital stays unavailable and risks forfeiture, so the attack has a real opportunity cost—whether the agents trade dune maps, ocean forecasts, or oasis water credits.
